headline: An 11-byte request that freezes OpenSSL servers, a Rust ransomware strain that locks a network in under a day, and a botnet ransacking exposed AI services headline a day defined by attacks on infrastructure trust.

emerging_trends.text: A Go botnet called NadMesh is scanning the internet for exposed AI services like Ollama and ComfyUI, harvesting thousands of cloud keys and Kubernetes tokens from teams that deploy AI tooling faster than they secure it.
emerging_trends.topic_title: NadMesh Botnet Hunts Exposed AI Services

emerging_trends.text: Ransomware crews keep compressing their timelines, with the new Rust-based Spirals strain racing from initial access to full network encryption in under 24 hours.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Spirals Ransomware Encrypts in Under 24 Hours

emerging_trends.text: Attackers are eroding the software trust chain from both ends, stealing code-signing certificates in the DigiCert breach while planting malicious npm packages that hide their command-and-control on blockchains.
emerging_trends.topic_title: GoldenEyeDog Linked to DigiCert Certificate Theft

topics.title: HollowByte Freezes OpenSSL Server Memory
topics.latest_developments: Okta's Red Team, which found and named the denial-of-service bug, published HollowByte's details on July 17, 2026, revealing that OpenSSL had quietly shipped the fix in June with no CVE, advisory, or changelog entry.
topics.summary: HollowByte lets an unauthenticated attacker send an 11-byte TLS request that makes an OpenSSL server reserve up to 131 KB of memory for a message that never arrives, and on glibc systems that memory stays gone until the process restarts. Any organization running an unpatched OpenSSL server faces denial of service and should apply the June fix.

sources.title: OpenSSL HollowByte Flaw Could Freeze Server Memory with 11-Byte TLS Requests
HollowByte DDoS flaw bloats OpenSSL server memory with 11-byte payload

topics.title: NadMesh Botnet Hunts Exposed AI Services
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News reported that NadMesh, a Go botnet that surfaced in early July 2026, scans Shodan for exposed AI services and that the operator's own dashboard claims 3,811 unique AWS keys.
topics.summary: NadMesh hunts ComfyUI, Ollama, n8n, Open WebUI, Langflow, and Gradio instances to steal cloud keys and Kubernetes tokens from teams that stand up AI tools fast and firewall them late. Organizations should lock down exposed model runners and workflow builders.

sources.title: New NadMesh Botnet Hunts Exposed AI Services for Cloud Keys and Kubernetes Tokens

topics.title: Spirals Ransomware Encrypts in Under 24 Hours
topics.latest_developments: Symantec's Threat Hunter Team disclosed Spirals, a previously unknown Rust ransomware that attackers deployed last month against an IT services company in South Asia, moving from initial access to data theft and full encryption in under 24 hours.
topics.summary: Spirals encrypts each file with a separate AES-128 key wrapped by an attacker-controlled ECDH key, making recovery without the operator impossible. The speed leaves defenders little time to detect and respond.

sources.title: Spirals ransomware locks down victim systems in under 24 hours

topics.title: ViteVenom npm Packages Use Blockchain C2
topics.latest_developments: Checkmarx uncovered ViteVenom, seven malicious npm packages targeting the Vite frontend tooling ecosystem that deliver a remote access trojan through a four-tier blockchain command-and-control spanning Tron and other chains, expanding the earlier ChainVeil campaign.
topics.summary: Developers who pull the poisoned Vite packages get a RAT, and the blockchain-based C2 makes takedown hard because attackers rotate infrastructure on-chain. Teams should audit npm dependencies and pin trusted versions.

sources.title: Seven Malicious Vite npm Packages Use Blockchain C2 to Deliver a RAT

topics.title: GoldenEyeDog Linked to DigiCert Certificate Theft
topics.latest_developments: Expel attributed the April 2026 DigiCert incident to CylindricalCanine, a sub-group of the Chinese group GoldenEyeDog, also tracked as APT-Q-27, Dragon Breath, and Miuuti Group, tying the breach to code-signing certificate theft.
topics.summary: GoldenEyeDog targets the gambling and gaming sectors, and stolen code-signing certificates let its operators sign malware that operating systems and users trust. Organizations should watch for abuse of DigiCert-issued certificates.

sources.title: GoldenEyeDog Subgroup Linked to DigiCert Breach and Code-Signing Certificate Theft

topics.title: EU Orders Google to Open Android to Rival AI
topics.latest_developments: The European Commission on July 17, 2026 ordered Google to give rival AI assistants the same Android reach Gemini enjoys—the camera, microphone, on-screen content, a display-off wake word, and background control of other apps—starting with Android 18 and fully by August 1, 2027.
topics.summary: The order reshapes how AI assistants reach Android hardware and raises fresh privacy and security questions about third-party assistants driving apps by imitating taps and typing. Regulators frame the move as competition enforcement.

sources.title: E.U. Orders Google to Open Android Mic, Camera and Screen to Rival AI Assistants

business_politics.title: U.S. Strikes Iran After Troop Deaths, Tehran Hits Gulf States
business_politics.latest_developments: U.S. Central Command launched fresh retaliatory strikes Saturday, July 18, and promised swift retaliation, while Iran for the first time hit U.S. Gulf allies—striking a Kuwaiti desalination plant—pushing the toll to 16 American service members killed and more than 430 wounded since the war began.
business_politics.summary: The war between the United States and Iran, centered on control of the Strait of Hormuz, widened Saturday as both sides bombed each other's infrastructure and military targets and Tehran opened fire on U.S. Gulf allies; an Iranian missile attack on a base in Jordan killed two American troops and left one missing.
